NGSS:HS-PS1-1.cc_advanced: I can use valence electron patterns to predict and explain the properties of an unfamiliar element and how it will bond.
NGSS:HS-PS1-1.cc_at_target: I can use the periodic table to predict relative properties of elements from the patterns of electrons in their outer energy level.
NGSS:HS-PS1-1.cc_approaching: I can find an element's group and period and say how many valence electrons it has, with a periodic table guide.
NGSS:HS-PS1-1.cc_emerging: I can find elements on the periodic table and identify metals and nonmetals, with support.

NGSS:HS-PS1-2.cc_advanced: I can predict products of reactions I have not seen before and revise my explanation when new data disagrees with it.
NGSS:HS-PS1-2.cc_at_target: I can construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction using outer electron states and periodic table trends.
NGSS:HS-PS1-2.cc_approaching: I can explain why sodium and chlorine form a compound using valence electrons, with a worked example.
NGSS:HS-PS1-2.cc_emerging: I can identify reactants and products in a simple chemical equation, with labels.

NGSS:HS-PS1-3.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation of melting points or solubility and use the results to rank attractive forces between particles in several substances.
NGSS:HS-PS1-3.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation comparing bulk properties of substances to infer the strength of electrical forces between particles.
NGSS:HS-PS1-3.cc_approaching: I can follow a procedure to compare melting or boiling points and say which substance has stronger forces, with support.
NGSS:HS-PS1-3.cc_emerging: I can describe physical properties such as melting point and hardness, using a word bank.

NGSS:HS-PS1-4.cc_advanced: I can use bond energy values to calculate whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic and explain the result with an energy diagram.
NGSS:HS-PS1-4.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to show that the energy released or absorbed in a reaction depends on changes in total bond energy.
NGSS:HS-PS1-4.cc_approaching: I can read an energy diagram and say if a reaction releases or absorbs energy, with guided questions.
NGSS:HS-PS1-4.cc_emerging: I can say that some reactions get hot and some get cold, using lab observations.

NGSS:HS-PS1-5.cc_advanced: I can use collision theory and data to predict how changing temperature and concentration together will affect a reaction rate.
NGSS:HS-PS1-5.cc_at_target: I can apply scientific principles and evidence to explain how changing temperature or concentration affects the rate of a reaction.
NGSS:HS-PS1-5.cc_approaching: I can describe from lab data that warmer or more concentrated solutions react faster, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-PS1-5.cc_emerging: I can time a simple reaction and say whether it was fast or slow, with help.

NGSS:HS-PS1-6.cc_advanced: I can apply Le Chatelier's principle to an industrial process, such as ammonia production, and justify the best conditions for product yield.
NGSS:HS-PS1-6.cc_at_target: I can refine the design of a chemical system by choosing a change in conditions that increases the amount of product at equilibrium.
NGSS:HS-PS1-6.cc_approaching: I can predict which way an equilibrium shifts when one condition changes, using a guide.
NGSS:HS-PS1-6.cc_emerging: I can describe that some reactions go both forward and backward, with a diagram.

NGSS:HS-PS1-7.cc_advanced: I can use mole ratios and mass data to show conservation of mass and calculate the mass of product from a given reactant.
NGSS:HS-PS1-7.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support the claim that atoms, and so mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.
NGSS:HS-PS1-7.cc_approaching: I can balance a simple chemical equation and count atoms on each side, with step-by-step support.
NGSS:HS-PS1-7.cc_emerging: I can count the atoms of each element in a chemical formula, with help.

NGSS:HS-PS1-8.cc_advanced: I can compare fission, fusion, and radioactive decay using nuclear equations and explain their uses and risks for energy production.
NGSS:HS-PS1-8.cc_at_target: I can develop models to show how the nucleus changes and energy is released during fission, fusion, and radioactive decay.
NGSS:HS-PS1-8.cc_approaching: I can use diagrams to describe the difference between fission and fusion, with a word bank.
NGSS:HS-PS1-8.cc_emerging: I can name protons and neutrons as particles in the nucleus, using a model.

NGSS:HS-PS2-1.cc_advanced: I can analyze motion data from a new situation, calculate net force, and predict acceleration using F = ma.
NGSS:HS-PS2-1.cc_at_target: I can analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law describes the relationship among net force, mass, and acceleration.
NGSS:HS-PS2-1.cc_approaching: I can use F = ma to solve a simple problem and read a velocity-time graph, with a worked example.
NGSS:HS-PS2-1.cc_emerging: I can say that a bigger force makes an object speed up more, using a demonstration.

NGSS:HS-PS2-2.cc_advanced: I can use momentum calculations to analyze a real collision, such as a car crash, and explain what the results show.
NGSS:HS-PS2-2.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support the claim that total momentum of a system is conserved when there is no net force.
NGSS:HS-PS2-2.cc_approaching: I can calculate momentum (p = mv) for objects before and after a collision, with support.
NGSS:HS-PS2-2.cc_emerging: I can say that heavier or faster objects are harder to stop, using examples.

NGSS:HS-PS2-3.cc_advanced: I can test and refine my collision device using data and explain how it reduces force by increasing collision time.
NGSS:HS-PS2-3.cc_at_target: I can apply science and engineering ideas to design, evaluate, and refine a device that minimizes force on an object during a collision.
NGSS:HS-PS2-3.cc_approaching: I can build a device such as an egg-drop container and describe how it protects the object, with a design template.
NGSS:HS-PS2-3.cc_emerging: I can name safety devices that protect people in crashes, such as seatbelts and helmets, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-PS2-4.cc_advanced: I can use both laws to compare gravitational and electric forces and predict how changing distance or mass or charge changes the force.
NGSS:HS-PS2-4.cc_at_target: I can use Newton's Law of Gravitation and Coulomb's Law to describe and predict gravitational and electrostatic forces between objects.
NGSS:HS-PS2-4.cc_approaching: I can use a formula with given values to calculate a gravitational or electric force, with a worked example.
NGSS:HS-PS2-4.cc_emerging: I can say that masses attract each other and that charges can attract or repel, using diagrams.

NGSS:HS-PS2-5.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation that shows both effects and apply them to explain how a generator or motor works.
NGSS:HS-PS2-5.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation to show that an electric current makes a magnetic field and a changing magnetic field makes a current.
NGSS:HS-PS2-5.cc_approaching: I can follow a lab procedure with a coil and compass to observe a magnetic effect from current, with support.
NGSS:HS-PS2-5.cc_emerging: I can build a simple circuit and say when current is flowing, with help.

NGSS:HS-PS2-6.cc_advanced: I can explain how the molecular structure of a designed material, such as a polymer, gives it a property and suggest a design improvement.
NGSS:HS-PS2-6.cc_at_target: I can communicate scientific and technical information about why molecular-level structure is important to how designed materials work.
NGSS:HS-PS2-6.cc_approaching: I can describe how one material's structure makes it strong or flexible, using a text and diagram with support.
NGSS:HS-PS2-6.cc_emerging: I can name everyday designed materials and one property of each, such as plastic is flexible.

NGSS:HS-PS3-1.cc_advanced: I can build a computational model, such as a spreadsheet, that tracks energy in a system and test it against real data.
NGSS:HS-PS3-1.cc_at_target: I can create a computational model to calculate the energy change of one part of a system when other energy changes and flows are known.
NGSS:HS-PS3-1.cc_approaching: I can use energy equations to calculate a missing energy value in a simple system, with a worked example.
NGSS:HS-PS3-1.cc_emerging: I can name forms of energy, such as kinetic, potential, and thermal, using examples.

NGSS:HS-PS3-2.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain energy changes at both the particle and object level in a real system, such as a pendulum or heated gas.
NGSS:HS-PS3-2.cc_at_target: I can develop and use models to show that energy can be explained as motion energy plus energy of relative position of particles or objects.
NGSS:HS-PS3-2.cc_approaching: I can label kinetic and potential energy at points on a roller coaster diagram, with support.
NGSS:HS-PS3-2.cc_emerging: I can say that moving objects have energy and raised objects have stored energy, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-PS3-3.cc_advanced: I can design, test, and refine an energy-converting device, calculate its efficiency, and justify design changes.
NGSS:HS-PS3-3.cc_at_target: I can design, build, and refine a device that works within constraints to convert one form of energy into another.
NGSS:HS-PS3-3.cc_approaching: I can build a device from a plan, such as a solar oven or simple motor, and describe the energy change, with support.
NGSS:HS-PS3-3.cc_emerging: I can name a device that changes energy from one form to another, such as a lamp.

NGSS:HS-PS3-4.cc_advanced: I can use calorimetry data to calculate heat transfer and explain how the results show the second law of thermodynamics.
NGSS:HS-PS3-4.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation to show that mixing objects at different temperatures in a closed system leads to a more even energy distribution.
NGSS:HS-PS3-4.cc_approaching: I can mix hot and cold water, record temperatures, and describe that they reach the same temperature, with support.
NGSS:HS-PS3-4.cc_emerging: I can say that heat moves from hot objects to cold objects, using a demonstration.

NGSS:HS-PS3-5.cc_advanced: I can use a field model to predict how forces and energy change as two charged or magnetic objects move closer or farther apart.
NGSS:HS-PS3-5.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model of two objects interacting through electric or magnetic fields to show the forces and energy changes.
NGSS:HS-PS3-5.cc_approaching: I can draw field lines between two magnets or charges and describe the force, with a diagram guide.
NGSS:HS-PS3-5.cc_emerging: I can observe that magnets push or pull each other without touching, with support.

NGSS:HS-PS4-1.cc_advanced: I can use the wave equation to solve problems in different media and explain why wave speed changes from air to water.
NGSS:HS-PS4-1.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support a claim about how frequency, wavelength, and speed of waves are related in different media.
NGSS:HS-PS4-1.cc_approaching: I can use v = f x wavelength to calculate one missing value, with a worked example.
NGSS:HS-PS4-1.cc_emerging: I can label wavelength and amplitude on a wave diagram, with a word bank.

NGSS:HS-PS4-2.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the advantages and drawbacks of digital storage and transmission, including security and data loss, using evidence.
NGSS:HS-PS4-2.cc_at_target: I can evaluate questions about the advantages of digital transmission and storage of information.
NGSS:HS-PS4-2.cc_approaching: I can list advantages of digital information, such as copying without loss, using a text with support.
NGSS:HS-PS4-2.cc_emerging: I can name devices that store digital information, such as phones and USB drives.

NGSS:HS-PS4-3.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from experiments such as the photoelectric effect and explain when the particle model or wave model is more useful.
NGSS:HS-PS4-3.cc_at_target: I can evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that light can be described by a wave model or a particle model, each useful in some situations.
NGSS:HS-PS4-3.cc_approaching: I can describe one piece of evidence for the wave model and one for the particle model of light, with support.
NGSS:HS-PS4-3.cc_emerging: I can say that light travels and can be reflected, using a demonstration.

NGSS:HS-PS4-4.cc_advanced: I can critique published claims about radiation, such as phone signals or UV light, and judge their reliability using scientific evidence.
NGSS:HS-PS4-4.cc_at_target: I can evaluate the validity and reliability of published claims about effects of different frequencies of electromagnetic radiation absorbed by matter.
NGSS:HS-PS4-4.cc_approaching: I can compare the energy of radio waves, UV, and X-rays and name one effect of each, using a chart.
NGSS:HS-PS4-4.cc_emerging: I can name types of electromagnetic radiation, such as light and X-rays, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-PS4-5.cc_advanced: I can explain in detail how a device such as a solar panel or fiber optic cable uses wave behavior, and suggest an improvement.
NGSS:HS-PS4-5.cc_at_target: I can communicate technical information about how devices use wave behavior and wave interactions with matter to send and capture information and energy.
NGSS:HS-PS4-5.cc_approaching: I can describe how one device, such as a phone or microwave, uses waves, using a diagram and sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-PS4-5.cc_emerging: I can name devices that use waves, such as radios and phones, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS1-1.cc_advanced: I can explain how a change in a DNA sequence changes a protein and affects a body function, using a real example such as sickle cell.
NGSS:HS-LS1-1.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how DNA structure determines protein structure, which carries out life functions in specialized cells.
NGSS:HS-LS1-1.cc_approaching: I can describe that DNA carries instructions to make proteins, using a diagram and word bank.
NGSS:HS-LS1-1.cc_emerging: I can say that DNA is found in the nucleus of cells, using a picture.

NGSS:HS-LS1-2.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how several body systems interact to respond to a challenge, such as exercise or illness.
NGSS:HS-LS1-2.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to show the hierarchy of interacting systems that perform specific functions in multicellular organisms.
NGSS:HS-LS1-2.cc_approaching: I can order cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems and give an example of each, with a graphic organizer.
NGSS:HS-LS1-2.cc_emerging: I can name major organs and say what they do, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS1-3.cc_advanced: I can design an investigation of a feedback mechanism, analyze the data, and explain how the body returns to balance.
NGSS:HS-LS1-3.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation to show that feedback mechanisms maintain homeostasis.
NGSS:HS-LS1-3.cc_approaching: I can measure heart rate before and after exercise and describe how the body returns to normal, with support.
NGSS:HS-LS1-3.cc_emerging: I can say that the body sweats to cool down and shivers to warm up, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS1-4.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how mitosis and differentiation build and repair tissues and what happens when division is uncontrolled.
NGSS:HS-LS1-4.cc_at_target: I can use a model to show the role of mitosis and differentiation in producing and maintaining complex organisms.
NGSS:HS-LS1-4.cc_approaching: I can put the stages of mitosis in order using diagrams and a word bank.
NGSS:HS-LS1-4.cc_emerging: I can say that cells divide to make new cells for growth and repair, using a picture.

NGSS:HS-LS1-5.cc_advanced: I can use a model to trace energy and matter through photosynthesis and explain how limiting factors affect its rate.
NGSS:HS-LS1-5.cc_at_target: I can use a model to show how photosynthesis changes light energy into stored chemical energy.
NGSS:HS-LS1-5.cc_approaching: I can label the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis on a diagram, with a word bank.
NGSS:HS-LS1-5.cc_emerging: I can say that plants use sunlight to make food, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS1-6.cc_advanced: I can trace atoms from sugar into proteins, fats, and other molecules and revise my explanation using new evidence.
NGSS:HS-LS1-6.cc_at_target: I can construct and revise an explanation for how carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugars combine with other elements to form large carbon-based molecules.
NGSS:HS-LS1-6.cc_approaching: I can identify carbohydrates, proteins, and fats and the elements they contain, using a chart.
NGSS:HS-LS1-6.cc_emerging: I can name foods that contain sugar, protein, or fat, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS1-7.cc_advanced: I can compare photosynthesis and cellular respiration as linked processes and explain the energy transfer in terms of bonds broken and formed.
NGSS:HS-LS1-7.cc_at_target: I can use a model to show that cellular respiration breaks bonds in food and oxygen and forms new compounds, transferring energy.
NGSS:HS-LS1-7.cc_approaching: I can label the inputs and outputs of cellular respiration on a diagram, with a word bank.
NGSS:HS-LS1-7.cc_emerging: I can say that our cells use food and oxygen to get energy, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS2-1.cc_advanced: I can use population data and a model to predict carrying capacity and explain how changing one factor shifts it.
NGSS:HS-LS2-1.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical or computational representations to support explanations of factors that affect carrying capacity of ecosystems.
NGSS:HS-LS2-1.cc_approaching: I can read a population graph and identify where it levels off at carrying capacity, with support.
NGSS:HS-LS2-1.cc_emerging: I can say that an area can only support a limited number of animals, using examples.

NGSS:HS-LS2-2.cc_advanced: I can analyze biodiversity data from different ecosystems, calculate changes, and revise my explanation based on new evidence.
NGSS:HS-LS2-2.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support and revise explanations about factors affecting biodiversity and populations in ecosystems.
NGSS:HS-LS2-2.cc_approaching: I can calculate a simple population change from data and name one factor that caused it, with support.
NGSS:HS-LS2-2.cc_emerging: I can count species in a sample area and record them in a table, with help.

NGSS:HS-LS2-3.cc_advanced: I can compare energy yield in aerobic and anaerobic conditions and explain real examples, such as muscle fatigue or bread making.
NGSS:HS-LS2-3.cc_at_target: I can construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for cycling of matter and flow of energy in aerobic and anaerobic conditions.
NGSS:HS-LS2-3.cc_approaching: I can describe the difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration using a chart, with support.
NGSS:HS-LS2-3.cc_emerging: I can say that most living things need oxygen to get energy from food.

NGSS:HS-LS2-4.cc_advanced: I can calculate energy transfer across trophic levels using the 10 percent rule and explain why food chains are short.
NGSS:HS-LS2-4.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support claims about cycling of matter and flow of energy among organisms in an ecosystem.
NGSS:HS-LS2-4.cc_approaching: I can use an energy pyramid to show that energy decreases at each level, with support.
NGSS:HS-LS2-4.cc_emerging: I can build a food chain and name producers and consumers, using picture cards.

NGSS:HS-LS2-5.cc_advanced: I can use a carbon cycle model to explain how burning fossil fuels and deforestation change carbon in each sphere.
NGSS:HS-LS2-5.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to show the role of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in cycling carbon among the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.
NGSS:HS-LS2-5.cc_approaching: I can complete a carbon cycle diagram showing where photosynthesis and respiration move carbon, with a word bank.
NGSS:HS-LS2-5.cc_emerging: I can say that plants take in carbon dioxide and animals breathe it out, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS2-6.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from a real ecosystem disturbance and argue whether it will recover or become a new ecosystem.
NGSS:HS-LS2-6.cc_at_target: I can evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that ecosystems stay stable in stable conditions but changing conditions can create a new ecosystem.
NGSS:HS-LS2-6.cc_approaching: I can use a case study to describe how an ecosystem changed after a disturbance, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-LS2-6.cc_emerging: I can name events that change ecosystems, such as floods and fires, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS2-7.cc_advanced: I can design, test, and refine a solution to a local biodiversity problem, such as protecting mangroves in Qatar, using data and trade-offs.
NGSS:HS-LS2-7.cc_at_target: I can design, evaluate, and refine a solution for reducing the impacts of human activities on the environment and biodiversity.
NGSS:HS-LS2-7.cc_approaching: I can propose a solution to a human impact on biodiversity and list its pros and cons, with a template.
NGSS:HS-LS2-7.cc_emerging: I can name human activities that harm the environment, such as pollution, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS2-8.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from studies of several species and explain how group behavior increases survival and reproduction.
NGSS:HS-LS2-8.cc_at_target: I can evaluate evidence for the role of group behavior in individuals' and species' chances to survive and reproduce.
NGSS:HS-LS2-8.cc_approaching: I can describe one example of group behavior, such as fish schooling, and how it helps survival, with support.
NGSS:HS-LS2-8.cc_emerging: I can name animals that live in groups, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS3-1.cc_advanced: I can ask and refine questions that connect genes, chromosomes, and proteins to explain how a specific trait is inherited.
NGSS:HS-LS3-1.cc_at_target: I can ask questions to clarify how DNA and chromosomes code instructions for traits passed from parents to offspring.
NGSS:HS-LS3-1.cc_approaching: I can ask a question about how traits are passed on and use a diagram of chromosomes to answer it, with question stems.
NGSS:HS-LS3-1.cc_emerging: I can say that children get traits from both parents, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS3-2.cc_advanced: I can defend a claim about which source of variation best explains a specific case, using evidence from meiosis, replication errors, or mutations.
NGSS:HS-LS3-2.cc_at_target: I can make and defend a claim with evidence that inheritable variation comes from meiosis, replication errors, or environmental mutations.
NGSS:HS-LS3-2.cc_approaching: I can describe one way new genetic variation happens, such as crossing over in meiosis, with a diagram.
NGSS:HS-LS3-2.cc_emerging: I can notice that siblings look different from each other, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS3-3.cc_advanced: I can use probability and population data to predict trait frequencies and explain differences between predicted and observed results.
NGSS:HS-LS3-3.cc_at_target: I can apply statistics and probability to explain the variation and distribution of expressed traits in a population.
NGSS:HS-LS3-3.cc_approaching: I can use a Punnett square to predict the chance of a trait, with a worked example.
NGSS:HS-LS3-3.cc_emerging: I can collect data on a trait, such as height, in my class and display it in a chart, with help.

NGSS:HS-LS4-1.cc_advanced: I can combine several lines of evidence, such as DNA, fossils, and anatomy, to argue for common ancestry of a group of organisms.
NGSS:HS-LS4-1.cc_at_target: I can communicate scientific information that common ancestry and evolution are supported by multiple lines of evidence.
NGSS:HS-LS4-1.cc_approaching: I can describe one line of evidence for evolution, such as fossils or similar bones, using sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-LS4-1.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils show living things from long ago, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-LS4-2.cc_advanced: I can use the four factors to explain evolution in a new example and predict how changing one factor would change the outcome.
NGSS:HS-LS4-2.cc_at_target: I can explain with evidence that evolution results from population growth potential, genetic variation, competition for resources, and better survival and reproduction.
NGSS:HS-LS4-2.cc_approaching: I can name the four factors of evolution and match each to an example, with a graphic organizer.
NGSS:HS-LS4-2.cc_emerging: I can say that animals compete for food and that some survive better than others.

NGSS:HS-LS4-3.cc_advanced: I can analyze data over generations to calculate changes in trait frequency and explain them using probability.
NGSS:HS-LS4-3.cc_at_target: I can apply statistics and probability to support explanations that organisms with helpful inherited traits increase in proportion over time.
NGSS:HS-LS4-3.cc_approaching: I can read a graph showing a trait increasing over generations and explain why, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-LS4-3.cc_emerging: I can count organisms with a trait in a simulation and record it, with help.

NGSS:HS-LS4-4.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how natural selection produced an adaptation in a real population, such as antibiotic resistance.
NGSS:HS-LS4-4.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural selection leads to adaptation of populations.
NGSS:HS-LS4-4.cc_approaching: I can describe an adaptation and how it helps an organism survive in its environment, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-LS4-4.cc_emerging: I can name an adaptation, such as a camel's hump, and say what it helps with.

NGSS:HS-LS4-5.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence from a real case to argue whether environmental change led to population growth, new species, or extinction.
NGSS:HS-LS4-5.cc_at_target: I can evaluate evidence that environmental changes may increase some species, produce new species, and cause others to go extinct.
NGSS:HS-LS4-5.cc_approaching: I can describe how one environmental change affected a species, using a case study and support.
NGSS:HS-LS4-5.cc_emerging: I can say that some animals have gone extinct, using pictures and examples.

NGSS:HS-LS4-6.cc_advanced: I can create and revise a simulation, test several solutions, and recommend the best way to protect a species using results.
NGSS:HS-LS4-6.cc_at_target: I can create or revise a simulation to test a solution that reduces harmful human impacts on biodiversity.
NGSS:HS-LS4-6.cc_approaching: I can run a given simulation, change one variable, and describe how it affected biodiversity, with support.
NGSS:HS-LS4-6.cc_emerging: I can name an endangered animal, such as the Arabian oryx, and one threat to it.

NGSS:HS-ESS1-1.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to model the sun's life cycle and explain how fusion energy travels to Earth and affects life.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-1.cc_at_target: I can develop a model based on evidence of the sun's life span and how nuclear fusion in its core releases energy that reaches Earth as radiation.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-1.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to describe that the sun makes energy by fusion and sends it to Earth as light, with support.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-1.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun is a star that gives Earth light and heat.

NGSS:HS-ESS1-2.cc_advanced: I can evaluate several pieces of evidence, such as redshift and cosmic background radiation, and explain how each supports the Big Bang theory.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-2.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation of the Big Bang theory based on evidence from light spectra, galaxy motion, and composition of matter.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-2.cc_approaching: I can describe one piece of evidence for the Big Bang, such as galaxies moving apart, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-2.cc_emerging: I can say that the universe is very old and very large, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-ESS1-3.cc_advanced: I can explain how stars of different masses produce different elements and connect this to elements found on Earth.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-3.cc_at_target: I can communicate scientific ideas about how stars produce elements during their life cycle.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-3.cc_approaching: I can describe the main stages in a star's life cycle using a diagram and word bank.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-3.cc_emerging: I can say that stars are born, change, and die, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-ESS1-4.cc_advanced: I can use Kepler's laws and data to predict the orbit of a planet or satellite and explain the results.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-4.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the solar system.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-4.cc_approaching: I can use a given formula or simulation to compare orbital periods of two planets, with support.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-4.cc_emerging: I can say that planets move around the sun in paths called orbits, using a model.

NGSS:HS-ESS1-5.cc_advanced: I can analyze rock age data across a mid-ocean ridge and use plate tectonics to explain the pattern and predict ages at new locations.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-5.cc_at_target: I can evaluate evidence of crust movement and the theory of plate tectonics to explain the ages of crustal rocks.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-5.cc_approaching: I can use a map to describe that rocks get older moving away from a mid-ocean ridge, with support.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-5.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's crust is broken into plates that move, using a map.

NGSS:HS-ESS1-6.cc_advanced: I can combine evidence from meteorites, moon rocks, and ancient Earth minerals to build a detailed account of Earth's early history.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-6.cc_at_target: I can apply reasoning and evidence from ancient Earth materials, meteorites, and other planets to construct an account of Earth's formation and early history.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-6.cc_approaching: I can describe one type of evidence scientists use to learn how old Earth is, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-ESS1-6.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is billions of years old, using a timeline with help.

NGSS:HS-ESS2-1.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how internal and surface processes together formed a specific feature, such as the Zagros Mountains.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-1.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to show how Earth's internal and surface processes at different scales form continental and ocean-floor features.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-1.cc_approaching: I can match landforms, such as mountains and trenches, to the plate movement that formed them, with a diagram.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-1.cc_emerging: I can name landforms such as mountains, valleys, and islands, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-ESS2-2.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to show a chain of feedbacks from one change, such as melting ice, and predict further effects.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-2.cc_at_target: I can analyze geoscience data to claim that one change to Earth's surface can create feedbacks that change other Earth systems.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-2.cc_approaching: I can describe how one change, like losing plants, affects another Earth system, using a cause-and-effect chart.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-2.cc_emerging: I can name Earth's systems: air, water, land, and living things, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-ESS2-3.cc_advanced: I can use seismic and heat evidence to model mantle convection and explain how it drives plate motion.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-3.cc_at_target: I can develop a model based on evidence of Earth's interior to describe how thermal convection cycles matter.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-3.cc_approaching: I can label Earth's layers and draw convection currents in the mantle, with a diagram guide.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-3.cc_emerging: I can name Earth's layers: crust, mantle, and core, using a model.

NGSS:HS-ESS2-4.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how changes in energy flow, such as greenhouse gases or orbital changes, caused past and present climate change.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-4.cc_at_target: I can use a model to describe how changes in energy flowing into and out of Earth's systems change climate.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-4.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram of the greenhouse effect to explain why Earth warms, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-4.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun's energy warms Earth, using a picture.

NGSS:HS-ESS2-5.cc_advanced: I can design and carry out an investigation of a property of water and explain how it causes weathering or erosion in the real world.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-5.cc_at_target: I can plan and conduct an investigation of the properties of water and their effects on Earth materials and surface processes.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-5.cc_approaching: I can follow a procedure to test how water affects rock or soil and record my observations, with support.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-5.cc_emerging: I can say that water can wear away rock and move soil, using a demonstration.

NGSS:HS-ESS2-6.cc_advanced: I can build a quantitative carbon model, use it to predict the effect of more emissions, and explain the limits of my model.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-6.cc_at_target: I can develop a quantitative model to describe the cycling of carbon among the hydrosphere, atmosphere, geosphere, and biosphere.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-6.cc_approaching: I can use data to show where carbon is stored and how it moves between spheres, with a diagram.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-6.cc_emerging: I can name places where carbon is found, such as air, oceans, and living things.

NGSS:HS-ESS2-7.cc_advanced: I can argue with evidence how one change in life, such as photosynthesis, changed Earth's systems, and how those changes affected life.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-7.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument based on evidence about how Earth's systems and life on Earth have changed together over time.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-7.cc_approaching: I can describe one way living things changed Earth, such as plants adding oxygen to air, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-ESS2-7.cc_emerging: I can say that living things depend on air, water, and land, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-ESS3-1.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how resources, hazards, and climate shaped human settlement in a region, such as the history of Qatar.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-1.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural resources, natural hazards, and climate change have influenced human activity.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-1.cc_approaching: I can describe how one resource or hazard affected where people live, using a case study and sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-1.cc_emerging: I can say that people live near water and other resources, using maps or pictures.

NGSS:HS-ESS3-2.cc_advanced: I can evaluate several energy or mineral resource solutions with cost-benefit data and recommend the best one with reasons.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-2.cc_at_target: I can evaluate competing design solutions for developing, managing, and using energy and mineral resources based on cost-benefit ratios.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-2.cc_approaching: I can compare two energy sources, such as solar and natural gas, using a pros and cons table.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-2.cc_emerging: I can sort energy sources into renewable and nonrenewable, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-ESS3-3.cc_advanced: I can build and run a simulation, test management choices, and explain how they affect people and biodiversity over time.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-3.cc_at_target: I can create a computational simulation to show relationships among natural resource management, sustainability of human populations, and biodiversity.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-3.cc_approaching: I can use a given simulation and change one management choice to see its effect, with support.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-3.cc_emerging: I can say that using too many resources can harm people and nature, using examples.

NGSS:HS-ESS3-4.cc_advanced: I can evaluate and refine a technology, such as desalination or carbon capture, using data on costs, benefits, and environmental impact.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-4.cc_at_target: I can evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-4.cc_approaching: I can describe how one technology reduces a human impact and list one benefit and one drawback, with support.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-4.cc_emerging: I can name technologies that help the environment, such as recycling machines or solar panels.

NGSS:HS-ESS3-5.cc_advanced: I can analyze climate model results and data to forecast regional change, such as in the Gulf, and explain the uncertainty in my forecast.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-5.cc_at_target: I can analyze geoscience data and climate model results to make an evidence-based forecast of climate change and its future impacts.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-5.cc_approaching: I can read a temperature graph and describe the trend and one likely impact, with sentence frames.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-5.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's average temperature is rising, using a simple graph.

NGSS:HS-ESS3-6.cc_advanced: I can use a computational model to show how a human activity changes several linked Earth systems and test a way to reduce the change.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-6.cc_at_target: I can use a computational representation to show relationships among Earth systems and how human activity is changing them.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-6.cc_approaching: I can use a given model or graph to describe how a human activity changes one Earth system, with support.
NGSS:HS-ESS3-6.cc_emerging: I can name ways people change the air, water, and land, using pictures.

NGSS:HS-ETS1-1.cc_advanced: I can analyze a global challenge, such as water scarcity, and write precise, measurable criteria and constraints that reflect different societal needs.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-1.cc_at_target: I can analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints that account for societal needs and wants.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-1.cc_approaching: I can describe a global problem and list some criteria and constraints for a solution, using a template.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-1.cc_emerging: I can name a big world problem, such as clean water, with support.

NGSS:HS-ETS1-2.cc_advanced: I can break a complex problem into smaller problems, design solutions for each, and explain how they work together.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-2.cc_at_target: I can design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it into smaller problems that can be solved through engineering.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-2.cc_approaching: I can break a problem into two or three smaller parts and suggest a solution for one part, with a graphic organizer.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-2.cc_emerging: I can describe a problem and one idea to solve it, with support.

NGSS:HS-ETS1-3.cc_advanced: I can evaluate several solutions using prioritized criteria and trade-offs and justify my choice, including social, cultural, and environmental impacts.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-3.cc_at_target: I can evaluate a solution to a complex problem using prioritized criteria and trade-offs, including cost, safety, reliability, aesthetics, and social and environmental impacts.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-3.cc_approaching: I can use a decision matrix to rate a solution against given criteria, with support.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-3.cc_emerging: I can say one good thing and one problem with a solution, using sentence frames.

NGSS:HS-ETS1-4.cc_advanced: I can build or modify a computer simulation, test several solutions, and explain how the results show interactions between systems.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-4.cc_at_target: I can use a computer simulation to model how proposed solutions to a complex problem affect interactions within and between systems.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-4.cc_approaching: I can run a given simulation with two solutions and compare the results, with step-by-step support.
NGSS:HS-ETS1-4.cc_emerging: I can use a simple simulation and describe what happens when I change one thing, with help.
